_notes: Single source for the Hotstrings card and the AutoHotkey script that the card's Apply button generates (autohotkey.script in config).
prompts: typed trigger pastes the text (instant, no ending key needed).
text: plain text; a newline means Enter, {me} is config owner_name. Fires after an ending key such as space, like a normal AutoHotkey hotstring.
hotkeys: 'send' is AutoHotkey Send syntax; 'app' limits the hotkey to that executable; 'action' is hibernate or clear (type /clear and press Enter, after 'before' keys).

prompts.label: Adversarial review
prompts.text: Review the change you just made as a sceptical senior reviewer whose job is to find what is wrong. Look for incorrect logic, unhandled edge cases, broken callers, security issues, and anything that contradicts what I asked for. List concrete findings with file:line and a failing scenario for each, most severe first. Do not fix anything yet.

prompts.label: Parallel implementations
prompts.text: Before choosing an approach, sketch two or three genuinely different ways to implement this, each in a few lines: the design, what it touches, and its main risk. Recommend one and say why, then implement only that one.

prompts.label: Loop until passing
prompts.text: Run the tests (or the check I named). If anything fails, read the failure, fix the root cause, and run them again. Keep looping until everything passes or you hit something you cannot fix without a decision from me; then stop and tell me exactly what is blocking. Never weaken or skip a test to make it pass.

prompts.label: Interview me
prompts.text: Before you start, interview me. Ask the questions whose answers would change what you build, one at a time, each with your recommended answer, until you are confident you understand what I want. Then summarise the plan in a few lines and wait for my go-ahead.

prompts.label: Plan before editing
prompts.text: Do not edit any files yet. Read the relevant code, then write a short plan: what you will change, in which files, in what order, and how you will verify it. Call out anything risky or uncertain. Wait for my approval before making changes.

prompts.label: Verify with evidence
prompts.text: Before you tell me this is done, prove it. Run the code, the tests or the app, and show me the actual output that demonstrates it works. If you could not verify something, say so plainly instead of assuming it works.

prompts.label: Root cause
prompts.text: Find the root cause before changing anything. Reproduce the problem, form a hypothesis, and confirm it with evidence such as logs, a failing test or a minimal reproduction. Then fix the cause rather than the symptom, and add a test that would have caught it.

prompts.label: Test first
prompts.text: Work test-first. Write a failing test that captures the behaviour I want, run it to see it fail for the right reason, then write the minimum code to make it pass. Refactor once it is green. Repeat for each behaviour.

prompts.label: Cut over engineering
prompts.text: This is more complicated than it needs to be. Simplify it: remove abstractions, options and layers nothing uses today, inline one-use helpers, and prefer the plainest code that does the job. Keep the behaviour identical and the tests green.

prompts.label: Assumptions first
prompts.text: Before writing any code, list the assumptions you are making about the requirements, the environment and the existing code. Mark which you have verified and which are guesses, and ask me about any guess that would change the design.

prompts.label: Session handoff
prompts.text: We are wrapping up this session. Write a handoff note for a fresh session: the goal, what is done, what is in progress, decisions made and why, open questions, and the exact next steps with file paths. Keep it concise and self-contained.

text.text: Good to speak with you earlier.
If there is any question or suggestion on this topic, please kindly contact me.

hotkeys.label: Clear current session: wipe the composer, then /clear
Clear current session: focus the Claude Code input, then /clear
